[Date]

To: [Health plan name and Appeals Department]  
[Appeals mailing address, fax number, or portal submission information]

Re: Appeal of denial for lumbar fusion  
Member: Jordan Jennings  
Member ID: W374276116  
Reference number: POC-7B726A30C1-53854  
Requested procedure: Lumbar fusion, CPT 22612  
Denial date: August 19, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria.

The medical records support medical necessity based on progressive symptoms, objective neurologic findings, documented functional impairment, imaging-confirmed structural disease, and failure of substantial conservative treatment:

- I have experienced 18 months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 24 supervised physical-therapy visits over 16 weeks, from April 9, 2026, through July 30, 2026. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility exercises. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this course of care.
- I used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 19, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- MRI and flexion-extension radiographs dated July 8, 2026, show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, together with severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- My symptoms are functionally disabling. I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. Sitting provides relief, which is consistent with neurogenic claudication.
- Examination documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.
- The records document no bowel or bladder dysfunction, but the absence of those symptoms does not eliminate the documented severe stenosis, nerve-related symptoms, sensory deficits, and major limitation in walking and standing.
- There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. My BMI is 29.

Taken together, these records show a persistent and worsening lumbar condition with radiographic instability, severe central stenosis, cauda-equina compression, bilateral L5 sensory findings, neurogenic claudication, and failure of extensive nonoperative treatment. The requested fusion is being recommended by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, to treat this documented lumbar pathology and associated functional impairment.

The denial does not identify the specific medical-necessity criteria that were applied or explain which requirement was allegedly not satisfied. I was unable to identify a payer-specific governing policy from the notice because the notice identifies only Texas Medicaid and does not name the Medicaid managed-care plan or other payer. The plan’s policy has therefore not been quoted in this appeal. Please provide the exact policy or clinical-review guideline used for this decision, including its title, policy number, version or effective date, the specific criteria applied to CPT 22612, and the clinical rationale for finding that the submitted records did not satisfy those criteria.

Please conduct a full reconsideration of the prior-authorization request, review all submitted clinical records, and overturn the denial. If the denial is upheld, please provide a detailed explanation identifying each unmet criterion, the medical evidence considered, the reviewer’s qualifications, and instructions for the next level of appeal or fair-hearing review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me if any additional information is required.

Sincerely,

Jordan Jennings  
Member ID: W374276116
